stem: The authority to determine the number of Judges in a High Court rests with which of the following entities?

options.label: b
options.text: The Chief Minister of the State

expl: Among the given options, the President has the authority to determine the number of judges in a High Court. According to Article 216, every High Court shall consist of a Chief Justice and such other Judges as the President may, from time to time, consider necessary to appoint.

stem: A High Court Judge addresses his letter of resignation to–

options.label: c
options.text: The Chief Justice of his High Court

expl: After taking the oath of office, a Judge of a High Court holds office until the age of 62 years. Before that, he may resign his office by a signed letter addressed to the President (Article 217(1)(a)). Also, on the ground of proved misbehaviour or incapacity, he may be removed by the President on an address by each House of Parliament, passed separately by a majority of the total membership of that House and supported by a majority of not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting.

stem: Which High Court stated that the divorce, by saying ‘Talaq’ 3 times, is illegal?
expl: In Rahmatullah and Khatoon Nisa vs. State of Uttar Pradesh & Others (1994), the Allahabad High Court held that a talaq given by saying “talaq” three times in a single sitting, with the intention of defeating the provisions of law, is illegal.

stem: What is the nature of the dispute of Babri Mosque/ Ramjanmabhoomi Case before Allahabad High Court?
expl: The Babri Masjid/Ram Janmabhoomi dispute was filed before the Allahabad High Court as a “title suit”, in which several parties made their respective claims over the land and property of the Babri Masjid/Ram Janmabhoomi site.
